biggest_catch: Microtask pay is cents per task and inventory varies; the $10 PayPal threshold takes many small tasks. Realistic sustained earnings are roughly $1-$2/hour, so the first $10 = about 5-10 hours of grinding. Boring and real, not fast money.
catches: Task pay is per microtask (cents); reaching the $10 PayPal minimum requires a large volume of tasks.
Task availability varies — the help center itself notes inventory can be low.
Accuracy matters; poor accuracy can lose access to tasks.
Payments go through a review batch: batched Tuesday, released Thursday (~48h later).
$10 minimum for PayPal withdrawals ($20+ for Bitcoin).
costs_and_unpaid_time: No monetary cost; free to join. Unpaid time: account setup, learning task instructions, tasks expired or rejected for accuracy, and waiting through the Tuesday-batch/Thursday-release payroll cycle.

c4.evidence: Official help center article https://help.hivemicro.com/hc/en-us/articles/360054656532-When-will-I-receive-my-Payroll loaded live 2026-09-23; Hive Work/Hive Micro is an established microtask platform with a public payroll process.

demand_side: Hive Work (Hive Micro) worker dashboard at hivemicro.com — the platform itself is the venue: requesters post microtasks (image labeling, transcription snippets, categorization, data validation) to the task feed. Users reach it today by free registration; tasks are self-serve (open the feed, pick an available task, follow instructions). Continued access depends on following instructions and maintaining accuracy; there is no interview, but low-accuracy workers lose task access.
eligibility: Anyone who can register a free Hive Work account; PayPal account needed for the $10 withdrawal tier.
maximize: Work the task feed during high-inventory periods; read instructions fully before starting (accuracy protects access); prefer tasks with the best pay-per-minute; let the balance cross $10 before the Tuesday batch so it releases that Thursday.
notes: Hive Micro has fully public official payroll terms — rare for microtask platforms. AI-proof angle is moderate: tasks are human-judgment microtasks (labeling, validation) that requesters specifically buy as human-labeled data, though individual tasks are simple. Realism: per-task pay is cents and not published officially; $1-$2/hour sustained is an honest estimate, so the $10 first payout = roughly 300-600 active minutes. A real person grinding several hours over a few days can plausibly hit $10 and see it released on Thursday.
numeric_basis: Official: $10 minimum PayPal withdrawal, Tuesday batch / Thursday release. Time range (300-600 active minutes) is an honest estimate from microtask economics (cents per task, ~$1-$2/hr sustained) — per-task rates are NOT published officially, flagged here rather than invented.

Your account must have a minimum balance of $10 for PayPal withdrawals and a minimum of $20 or more as you set for Bitcoin transactions to be eligible for payout.
payout_value_note: $10 is the minimum PayPal withdrawal threshold, not per-task pay. Individual microtasks pay cents (rates not published officially).

steps: Create a free Hive Work (Hive Micro) account.
Open the task feed and complete microtasks, following instructions carefully to protect accuracy.
Keep working until the account balance reaches at least $10.
No manual request needed — qualifying balances are batched Tuesday 12:00 AM GMT.
Receive the PayPal payment around 48 hours later on Thursday after payment review.
timing: Payments batched every Tuesday (12:00 AM GMT), released ~48 hours later on Thursday.
what_gets_accepted: Microtasks completed per instructions with acceptable accuracy; payments pass a batch review before release.
when_cash_arrives: PayPal around Thursday (48 hours after the Tuesday batch), once the $10 minimum is met.
who_pays: Hive Work / Hive Micro (funded by requesters who buy human-labeled microtask data).
who_qualifies: Any adult who can follow written task instructions accurately — the work requires real human judgment on individual data items (images, text snippets), which is what requesters are buying rather than AI labels.
work_available: Self-serve task feed; the help center notes availability can be low at times and accuracy affects continued access — 'unverified' day-to-day volume.
